decision.question: Where is DOOR_RETRO_ELIGIBILITY resolved and how do the three doors (door_where SQL, bundle._member_door_ok, GraphExecutor.door_filter) share that shield decision without drifting apart?

plans.title: Helper read on every call in door.py
plans.stance: door.py owns a retro_shield() helper that reads os.environ on each call, and all three doors import it and apply their own currently_eligible check.
plans.summary: Add currently_eligible boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true to temporal tables in db.create_chunk_table, write it from the 5-tuple in retriever_pg.index_temporal, and derive it in history_sim from the final segment state. door.py gains retro_shield(); door_where appends 'AND currently_eligible = true' for non-audit temporal queries under shield; _member_door_ok gains currently_eligible (after currently_privileged) and _neighbor_info selects it; door_filter aggregates bool_and(currently_eligible) and drops docs with any ineligible row. Extend test_door/test_temporal_bundles/test_temporal_graph with monkeypatch.setenv, and add docs/retro-eligibility-policy.md plus README notes on the switch and the index rebuild.

plans.title: Constant read when door.py loads
plans.stance: Read the setting once into a door.py module constant, following db.py's HOST/PORT pattern, and have every door check that constant.
plans.summary: Same schema, indexing and history_sim changes as Plan 1, but door.py defines RETRO_ELIGIBILITY = os.environ.get('DOOR_RETRO_ELIGIBILITY', '') at import, and door_where, _member_door_ok and door_filter check door.RETRO_ELIGIBILITY == 'shield'. Tests monkeypatch harness.door.RETRO_ELIGIBILITY rather than the environment. The policy doc says a restart is needed to change modes, alongside the index rebuild.

plans.title: Field on QueryContext
plans.stance: Carry the policy on QueryContext as a retro_eligibility field whose default comes from the environment, so each door reads it from the context just as it reads temporal_mode.
plans.summary: Add retro_eligibility: str = field(default_factory=lambda: os.environ.get('DOOR_RETRO_ELIGIBILITY', '')) to ports.QueryContext, documented next to temporal_mode, and keep it out of models.SearchRequest so clients cannot override it. door_where, _member_door_ok (new currently_eligible parameter) and door_filter check context.retro_eligibility == 'shield' and not audit; schema, index_temporal 5-tuple and history_sim changes match Plan 1. Tests build QueryContext(retro_eligibility='shield') directly and also cover the env default, plus the policy doc and README updates.

plans.title: One Python decision function in door.py
plans.stance: Move the whole Python-side door decision, including shield, into a single door.door_ok function that bundle and graph_exec both call, alongside door_where for SQL.
plans.summary: door.py gains door_ok(eligibility, is_privileged, currently_privileged, currently_eligible, context, temporal), which reads DOOR_RETRO_ELIGIBILITY on each call, and door_where adds the matching currently_eligible predicate. bundle._member_door_ok keeps its required signature but just delegates to door_ok; graph_exec.door_filter selects bool_and(eligibility='eligible'), bool_or(is_privileged), bool_or(currently_privileged), bool_and(currently_eligible) and passes each doc's aggregates to door_ok, removing its inline rules. Schema, index_temporal, history_sim, tests, policy doc and README as in Plan 1.
